newsitem.title: USA: Sun enters $50 billion data center market.
newsitem.headline: Sun enters $50 billion data center market.

text.p: Sun Microsystems Inc. on Wednesday unveiled its first mainframe-class server computer, which it said marks its entry into a $50 billion market for data centre computer hardware, storage, software and services.

Ed Zander, president of the company's Sun Microsystems Computer Company, told a gathering of analysts, customers and reporters at San Francisco's Museum of Modern Art, he expected the machines to sell for an average price of over $1 million.
Servers are computers that manage the flow of data in a network.

Zander said the new Ultra Enterprise 10000 servers, which can compete with mainframe computers on many measurements of computing performance, will have a longer sales cycle than Sun's more traditional Unix product lines.
He also said Sun expects to sell more of its speedy Ultra Enterprise 5000 and 6000 midrange servers as a result of its new high-end machine, which will begin shipping in volume in March.

"It really puts Sun into some new markets where they have not been able to play before," said C.B. Lee, senior analyst at Sutro & Co. While some potential customers may be initially sceptical, it can help usher Sun into company's data centres.

Lee said the new server would be most useful for running complex database applications and for extending new computing capabilities, rather than replacing older software and hardware which have come to be known as legacy systems.
Sun said its 10000 series, codenamed 'Starfire', offers up to four times the performance of IBM's CMOS (complementary metal oxide semiconductor) mainframe and HP T-series servers.
The base Starfire configuration -- 16 processors and two gigabytes of memory -- will be priced around $870,000.
